# edgecenter_websec_lecert (Resource)

WebSec automated certificate: a certificate that the server issues and renews for an `edgecenter_websec_resource`, from Let's Encrypt or another ACME authority (see `cert_type`). A resource has at most one such certificate, so the id is the resource id.

Create waits until the server applies the resource and its `status` is no longer `processed`, then requests the certificate and waits until the request ends. A resource with `active` or `enabled` off is not waited for: the server refuses the request at once. The authority checks the domain of the resource over HTTP, so it has to resolve to its `protected_ip`: apply this resource after DNS points there. The certificate covers the domain only, not the subdomains of the resource. The server repeats a failed check after a pause and Create keeps waiting: raise `timeouts.create` if the domain needs time to resolve. A resource that uses its own `ssl_certificate` is refused: remove the attribute from the resource in the same apply.

A request that the server ends without a certificate is reported with its reason, and the certificate is marked tainted, so the next apply cleans up and requests it again. When the create timeout runs out first, the error shows the reason of the last failed check and the request keeps running; the next apply also replaces a certificate issued after the timeout, `terraform untaint` keeps it.

The server renews the certificate only while `active` and `enabled` of the resource are true and its `status` is `active`.

Destroy cancels a running request and revokes the certificate. Turn off the `redirect_http_to_https` option of the resource first: the revoke does not check it, and the site would redirect to HTTPS without a certificate.

Changing `resource_id` or `cert_type` replaces the certificate.

Import with `<resource_id>`. A resource moved from the old protection API keeps its id, so a Let's Encrypt certificate of `edgecenter_protection_resource_certificate` is imported here by the id from the old state.

## Example Usage

```terraform
provider "edgecenter" {
  permanent_api_token = "251$d3361.............1b35f26d8"
}

resource "edgecenter_websec_lecert" "example_com" {
  resource_id = 12345
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `resource_id` (Number) ID of the `edgecenter_websec_resource` to issue the certificate for. Changing it replaces the certificate.

### Optional

- `cert_type` (String) ACME authority that issues the certificate: `LE` (Let's Encrypt), `MDDC` or `EC`. `MDDC` and `EC` have to be enabled for the client, and `MDDC` is issued only for a resource without subdomains. Changing it replaces the certificate: the old one is revoked before the new request starts, so the site has no HTTPS until the new certificate is issued, and no certificate at all if the request fails. `create_before_destroy` does not help because a resource cannot get a second automated certificate. The type is read from the status of the last issue request. When the API keeps no request for the resource, as for a certificate moved from the old protection API, an imported certificate counts as `LE`. Defaults to `LE`.
- `timeouts` (Block, Optional) (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--timeouts))

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) The ID of this resource.
- `issue_error` (String) Error and details of that status, empty when the status carries none.
- `issue_status` (String) Latest status of the last issue request: `PROCESSING`, `DONE`, `FAILED`, `CANCELLED` or `FORBIDDEN`. Empty when the request has no status yet or the API keeps no request for the resource.
- `ssl_certificate` (Number) ID of the automated certificate attached to the resource, 0 until the first one is issued.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
terraform import edgecenter_websec_lecert.example_com 12345
```
